Roughly, the process relies on using a device that allows a photon to pass freely through a slit but forces its spin axis to point in a particular direction. If the devices in front of the left and right slits manipulate the photon spins in specific but dis tinct ways, then a more refined detector screen that not only registers a dot at the photon's impact location, but also keeps a record of the photon's spin orientation, will reveal through which slit a given photon passed on its way to the detector. When this double-slit-with-tagging experiment is run, the photons do not build up an interference pattern, as in Figure 7. 4a.
